title: Accelerating the Adoption of Software and AI Agent Identity and Authorization
relevance: Treats software-agent identification, authorization, and authority as a current problem that is broader than authenticating the hosting workload.

title: Zero Trust Architecture (SP 800-207)
relevance: Requires dynamic per-request policy using identity plus resource, device, and contextual data, qualifying identity-centric interpretations.

title: A Zero Trust Architecture Model for Access Control in Cloud-Native Applications in Multi-Cloud Environments (SP 800-207A)
relevance: Names SPIFFE as identity infrastructure while also requiring identity-tier and network-tier policies and telemetry.

title: SLSA v1.2 Provenance
relevance: Formalizes software artifact provenance beyond the book's practitioner treatment.

title: SLSA v1.2 Verifying Artifacts
relevance: Emphasizes that provenance has limited value unless consumers verify it against policy.

title: Principles and Approaches for Secure by Design Software
relevance: Moves responsibility toward manufacturers and executive leadership, broadening the book's internal engineering model.

title: SPIFFE Workload Endpoint Specification
relevance: Current specification details post-2020 endpoint and token behavior; it supersedes the book for normative implementation details.

title: Guidelines for Secure AI System Development
relevance: Adds AI-specific lifecycle, supply-chain, accountability, monitoring, and secure-operation expectations absent from the 2020 book.
